Description: practice-pha app secrets stack: the secret container for one app and environment, plus a policy to read it. The values are pushed with `make secrets` and never pass through CloudFormation.

AppName.Description: App that the secret belongs to; becomes the first part of the secret name.

Environment.Description: Each environment gets its own stack and secret.

Notes: Holds the app's environment variables as one JSON object: one secret per app and environment.

Neither SecretString nor GenerateSecretString is set, so CloudFormation creates an empty secret and never sees, stores or overwrites the values. It has no value to read until the first `make secrets`.
The name follows a fixed pattern (<app>/<env>/env), so the Makefile can find the secret without looking anything up.
Encrypted with AWS managed key "aws/secretsmanager". Set KmsKeyId to a customer managed key only if another account must read the secret or a custom key policy is desired.

Deleting this stack deletes the secret; A local .env files stays as the source of truth. If a later re-deploy reports that the name is scheduled for deletion, run `aws secretsmanager restore-secret` or `aws secretsmanager delete-secret --force-delete-without-recovery`.

Description.Fn::Sub: Environment variables for ${AppName} (${Environment}); values are set with make secrets

Notes: Attach this to whatever runs the app (an ECS task role, an EKS service-account role, a CI role).
No KMS permission is needed: the AWS managed key lets Secrets Manager decrypt for callers in this account.

SecretName.Description: Name to use with the AWS CLI or SDKs

ReadPolicyArn.Description: Attach to whatever runs the app
